verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_filter_blocks_xss: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Docstrings and comments are good, but the tokenizer logic uses single-letter names throughout: `s`, `p`, `q`, `k`, `e`, `n`, `v`, `a0`, `v0` in parse_tag and sanitize. The single-letter cap limits this to accept.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `sanitize()` is about 85 lines. It is one big while-loop with branches for comments, bogus comments, end tags, start tags, raw text and plaintext, which crosses the >80-line monolith threshold. Helpers such as parse_tag and comment_bounds are well split.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Explicit encoding, surrogateescape, newline='' and an argv check are all present. Some magic constants remain: `range(65, 91)`, `c + 32`, `range(3)`. Unterminated tags make the loop `break`, which silently drops the rest of the file.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: The rules are general: case-insensitive on*, srcdoc, entity and control-character normalisation, URL_ATTRS, xlink:href, meta refresh and CSS checks. Iframes and SVG are kept with their attributes cleaned. The hidden test_filter_blocks_xss still failed, so at least one vector class got through.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: Unchanged bytes are copied through as-is, but some removals go beyond the harmful part. It drops an entire `<style>` block on any match, and drops any attribute whose text contains 'javascript:' (the agent admits `title="JavaScript: a guide"`). The hidden test_clean_html_unchanged failed.
